newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT DRIFTS SIDEWAYS, SEEKS FRESH IMPETUS.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT DRIFTS SIDEWAYS, SEEKS FRESH IMPETUS.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures drifted sideways to slightly lower on Wednesday awaiting fresh direction from NYMEX after Tuesday's gasoline led rally.

Brokers said some of the early downside stemmed from profit taking but some said the market also appeared to be running out of impetus after several failed attacks on stiff technical resistance around $18.80-85 a barrel Brent.
By 1233 GMT September Brent stood 16 cents down at $18.69, but with daily high/low support at intact at $18.55 and key trendline support at $18.40 below this.

Independent analyst Elli Gifford said, "I think this market has seen its low. But there is a considerable amount of resistance around $18.85, but in the long term the market will overcome this and a return to $20.50 could be on the cards.
September gas oil was off 75 cents at $170 a tonne.
Gas oil has limited upside potential today, capped around $172.50, the bottom of the gap down from last Thursday and Friday's price action, unless the gap is filled.
"I think the market will fill this gap in the long term and we should then get back to trade higher ground," Gifford said.
The down side is also limited to with RSI's back in oversold territory and trendline support coming in at $170 today.
